By definition, an `INNER JOIN` returns only the rows where there is a match in both tables based on the join condition. If a row in the left table has no corresponding match in the right table, it is excluded from the result set.

The behavior you are describing—keeping all rows from the left table and returning `NULL` values for the right table's columns when there is no match—is the exact behavior of a `LEFT JOIN` (or `LEFT OUTER JOIN`). 

If your PR review is based on the premise that `INNER JOIN` keeps unmatched left rows, it will be rejected by anyone verifying the SQL standard.
